title: Create lightweight formatting template for Security Enablement one-pagers (Drive PDF + Confluence)
creator: Soojin Lee
description:
## Goal
Create a consistent, lightweight formatting template for customer-facing security/compliance one-pagers that:
- reads cleanly in PDF (Drive exports)
- can be reproduced in Confluence with minimal drift
- supports tables + callouts for “Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private” differences
- includes a footer version stamp (version + last reviewed + owner)

This is packaging/formatting only (no content rewrites beyond minor clarity edits needed to fit the layout).

## Background
Field feedback: one-pagers are being forwarded in late-stage cycles. Current drafts vary in structure and are hard to skim during security reviews. We need a repeatable pattern so Sales/SEs can quickly assemble a pack and customers can find the same info in Confluence (canonical) without the formatting changing meaning.

## Deliverables
1) One-pager layout template (PDF-friendly)
2) Confluence-friendly variant guidelines (what maps to what)
3) Components:
   - header block
   - section headings
   - “at-a-glance” summary
   - deployment mode comparison table (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
   - callout styles (Info / Customer action / Restricted note)
   - evidence pointer block (safe customer-facing version)
   - footer version stamp

## Template structure (standard)
### Header
- Title (e.g., “Audit Logging Overview”)
- Subtitle (1 line): what this doc covers / doesn’t cover
- Audience: Security / GRC / IT

### At-a-glance (max 5 bullets)
- “What you get”
- “What you configure”
- “Where it applies” (Hosted / Dedicated / Private)

### Core sections (recommended)
1. Overview
2. How it works (high level)
3. Configuration & options
4. Deployment mode differences (table)
5. FAQ / Common questions (optional)
6. Evidence & further reading (links)

## Tables
### Deployment mode comparison table
- 3 columns: Hosted | Dedicated | Private
- Rows vary per one-pager, but defaults to:
  - Data plane location
  - Control plane access
  - Customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM)
  - Audit log access/export
  - Retention controls
  - Shared responsibility notes

Rules:
- Keep each cell <= 2 lines when possible.
- Use consistent row names across one-pagers so readers can scan.
- Avoid absolutes (“always/never”) unless contractually true.

## Callouts
### Callout types
- Info (neutral): clarifications, definitions
- Customer action (highlight): “Customer must…” / “Customer may configure…”
- Restricted (internal only): NOT for customer PDFs; Confluence page can include a restricted-only block via page permissions

Copy rules:
- Callouts must be factual and product-accurate; no roadmap commitments.
- If something is contract-dependent, use: “Subject to contract and support tier.”

## Evidence pointers block
Customer-facing block:
- “SOC 2 Report: Available under NDA upon request via Redwood GRC.”
- “Pen test summary: Available upon request; scope varies by period.”
- “Subprocessor list: Available at [public link or ‘available upon request’ depending on page].”

Do NOT include internal doc links in customer PDFs.

## Footer version stamp (required)
Footer (right-aligned):
- Version: vX.Y
- Last reviewed: YYYY-MM-DD
- Owner: Security & Compliance PM
- Doc classification: “Customer-facing”

Format example:
“v2.0 • Last reviewed 2026-01-28 • Owner: Security & Compliance PM • Customer-facing”

## Confluence mapping guidance
- Header: Confluence page title + short excerpt
- At-a-glance: use a bullet list under an “At a glance” H2
- Callouts: Confluence “Info panel” for Info; “Note panel” for Customer action (title: “Customer action”)
- Tables: standard Confluence tables (avoid nested tables)
- Footer stamp: add a final section “Document metadata” with the version stamp text (keeps parity with PDFs)

## Assets / Links
- Drive template (slides): https://drive.google.com/ (placeholder)
- Confluence component examples: https://confluence.redwoodinference.com/ (placeholder)
- Used by: “Compliance one-pagers pack v2” + Security FAQ v2 appendix references

## Acceptance criteria
- AEs/SEs can paste content into the template with <15 minutes per one-pager.
- PDF export is readable (no reflow issues, tables don’t break across pages unexpectedly).
- Confluence reproduction is consistent enough that reviewers can diff meaningfully.
- Footer version stamp appears on every page.

## Open questions
- Do we need a 1-page maximum constraint? (Proposal: prefer 1 page; allow 2 for RBAC/SSO and Audit Logging if required.)
- Evidence pointer block: confirm final “safe language” with Olga (GRC) and Naomi (PM).

## Notes
This ticket covers formatting only. Content accuracy remains owned by Security & Compliance reviewers (Marcus/Olga/Naomi).
comments: 2026-01-17 (Soojin Lee): Please keep the template intentionally minimal—field will not adopt something that feels like a “marketing deck.” Skimmable + factual wins. Add a strong deployment mode table component; that’s the most common confusion point.

2026-01-20 (Elliot Price): Confluence parity request: avoid custom fonts/colors that won’t translate. If we rely on callouts, use Confluence-native panels. Also, footer stamp should be a final “Document metadata” section since Confluence doesn’t support true footers consistently.

2026-01-22 (Naomi Feldman): Ensure there is a place for “contract-dependent” caveats (esp incident notification / retention). Callout type for “Customer action” is helpful. Keep evidence pointers generic (no internal links).

2026-01-24 (Wei Chen): Draft template is ready in Slides. Tables are stable on PDF export; long cells wrap to 2 lines max. Added a strict header + at-a-glance pattern so one-pagers remain consistent across authors.
2026-01-28 (Soojin Lee): Approved. Please apply to the one-pagers pack and lock the master template in the Shared Drive. Reminder: export PDFs with embedded fonts + include version stamp per page.
final_outcome: Template delivered and approved. Slides master created for Drive PDF exports; Confluence mapping guidance documented. Components include deployment-mode comparison table, callout styles, evidence pointer block, and mandatory footer version stamp.
